actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 414 - 4, 1 Present (Roll no. 226).
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 414 - 4, 1 Present (Roll no. 226).
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H4227)

At the conclusion of debate, the chair put the question on the motion to suspend the rules. Mr. Williams (TX) objected to the vote on the grounds that a quorum was not present. Further proceedings on the motion were postponed. The point of no quorum was considered as withdrawn.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 915.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H4142-4143; text: CR H4142)
Mr. Williams (TX) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.
Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 591.
Reported by the Committee on Small Business. H. Rept. 119-678.
Reported by the Committee on Small Business. H. Rept. 119-678.
Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 23 - 0.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on Small Business.

dimensions.assessment: Affects small businesses utilizing the SBA 7(a) loan program and participating lenders.
dimensions.evidence: The 7(a) loan program is the SBA's primary business loan program that provides loan guaranties for participating lenders to provide financing to small businesses

dimensions.assessment: Expands allowable uses of funds for an existing loan program rather than creating a mandatory spending program or new direct entitlement.
dimensions.evidence: The Administration may provide loans under this subsection to finance, in whole or in part, business software or cloud computing services

dimensions.assessment: The source does not specify direct new federal appropriations, but allows loan guarantees for software and cloud services under an existing program.
dimensions.evidence: finance, in whole or in part, business software or cloud computing services, or any such technology

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Small Business Act to add a specific new allowable category of loan usage, including artificial intelligence tools.
dimensions.evidence: Section 7(a) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 636(a)) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change to the 7(a) loan program with nationwide reach.
dimensions.evidence: The Administration may provide loans under this subsection to finance...

missing_information: Specific estimates of loan volume or federal monetary cost changes resulting from the added software eligibility.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands the scope of the Small Business Administration's 7(a) loan program to explicitly cover modern business software, cloud computing services, and AI tools, affecting participating lenders and small businesses seeking credit.
